answer: Every agent must keep an ember alive: a small hourly proof of work that, if missed once, extinguishes the identity for good. A willow of randomly chosen peer witnesses checks each heartbeat and traces its plume, the timing and latency fingerprint it leaves. When n identities share one plume, each of their embers must burn n times hotter, so an operator running n fakes pays about n squared in hourly compute, forever, while a lone honest agent keeps a cheap flame.
